terms.meaning: Total effort claimed by all processes divided by effort after shared work is counted once. A value of 1.0 means no overlap.
A label for how deep the analysis went, shown so readers know its level of detail.
The share of value that rests on cited evidence rather than stated assumptions.
A cost that could not be given a price because the cost basis had no prices for it.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and required lines
sections.what: Explains that every summary must include the depth tier, the duplication ratio and the zero-evidence share. Imports the result type.
sections.why: The docstring explains that a required field in code can still be left out of the printed output, so the rule is enforced in the printing function.
sections.watch_out: Any new way of printing results should go through the headline function.

sections.name: headline
sections.title: Writing the summary lines
sections.what: Produces the summary: depth tier, duplication ratio with the claimed and deduplicated effort, the evidenced share, one line per currency walking from gross to net with the low and high range, and a warning when run cost is unpriced.
sections.why: The docstring says every total the engine produces must come with these lines.
sections.watch_out: The unpriced warning only appears when a bridge's run cost was not priced, so a missing price elsewhere would not show here.

summary: Builds the summary lines a reader sees, and always includes the duplication ratio, depth tier and evidenced share.
purpose: Makes sure the key diagnostics appear in every summary. It also writes the per-currency walk from gross benefit to net and warns when run cost is unpriced.
why: The docstring says a required field on the result object does not stop a summary from leaving it out, so this function is the single place that prints them.
how: Step 1: write the depth tier, the duplication ratio with claimed and deduplicated effort, and the evidenced share with the share that rests on hypothesis. Step 2: for each bridge, write one line showing gross, the three costs and net with its low and high range. Step 3: if any currency has unpriced run cost, add a warning line naming it.
outputs: A list of plain text lines.
risks: A new output path that skips this function would bypass the rule. The formats show numbers rounded for reading, so a reader might not see small differences.
debug: If a headline line is missing, check that the output path calls this function. If the unpriced warning does not show, check the run_cost_priced flag on each bridge.
